title: Database & data on mobile
content:
## Shared fundamentals

Mobile apps built on Emergent use the same MongoDB backend as web apps. The database URL model, storage limits, and core behavior are identical across platforms.

For a complete explanation of how database URLs work, connection strings, storage quotas, and data persistence, see the [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) page.

Key points for mobile:

- Each Emergent app gets a dedicated MongoDB cluster with a unique connection string
- The database is hosted remotely and accessed over HTTPS — your mobile app talks to the same cloud database as the web version
- All CRUD operations, indexes, and collections work identically on iOS, Android, and web

<Note>
Mobile apps do **not** bundle a local database. All data lives in the cloud MongoDB instance provisioned for your app.
</Note>

## Republish as an update

When you modify your mobile app's backend, database schema, or business logic and want to push that change to users, you must **republish** the app to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store as a new version.

Unlike web apps (which update instantly on the next page load), mobile apps are distributed as signed binaries with fixed bundle IDs. Any change to the backend — even a database migration or API endpoint tweak — requires:

<Steps>
<Step title="Rebuild the mobile app">
Trigger a new build in Emergent. The agent will increment the version number and compile fresh iOS/Android binaries.
</Step>

<Step title="Submit to the stores">
Upload the new build to App Store Connect (iOS) and Google Play Console (Android). Both stores will review the update.
</Step>

<Step title="Users receive the update">
Once approved, existing users see an "Update available" prompt in their store app. The new version downloads and replaces the old binary.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning title="No instant rollout">
There is no "hot reload" or instant deployment for mobile. Plan for store review times (hours to days) and user adoption lag (days to weeks).
</Warning>

**Database implications:**  
The database itself does **not** redeploy. The same MongoDB cluster persists across versions. When you republish:

- Existing user data remains intact
- Schema changes (new collections, fields, indexes) take effect immediately on the backend
- Old app versions still in the wild will continue querying the *updated* database — ensure backward compatibility or force a minimum version

## Fork into a new app

Instead of updating your published app, you can **fork** it into a separate app with its own identity and database.

A fork creates:

- A new Emergent project in your workspace
- A new bundle ID / package name (e.g., `com.yourcompany.myapp-v2`)
- A new, empty MongoDB cluster (no data copied from the original)
- Independent build artifacts for iOS and Android

**When to fork:**

- You want to launch a "Pro" or region-specific variant without affecting the original
- You're testing a major refactor and need a parallel app
- You want a clean slate for data (no migration path needed)

**How to fork:**

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the app's overflow menu">
In the workspace, find the mobile app card and click the **⋮** menu.
</Step>

<Step title="Select Fork">
Choose **Fork into new app**. Emergent will clone the codebase and create a new project.
</Step>

<Step title="Change the bundle ID">
Before building, update the bundle/package ID in the app settings to avoid conflicts with the original.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info" title="Forked apps are independent">
The fork does **not** share a database, deployment pipeline, or store listing with the original. You'll submit it as a brand-new app to Apple and Google.
</Callout>

## What carries over

How your database and user data are affected depends on whether you **update** (republish) or **fork**.

| Action | Database | User data | Bundle ID | Store listing |
|--------|----------|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| **Republish (update)** | Same cluster, schema changes apply | Persists; all users keep their data | Unchanged | Same app, new version number |
| **Fork** | New, empty cluster | None; starts blank | New ID required | New app submission |

**Republish:**
- Database connection string stays the same
- Existing collections and documents remain
- Schema migrations (new fields, indexes) affect all app versions immediately
- Users who haven't updated yet will query the *new* schema — plan for backward compatibility

**Fork:**
- You get a fresh MongoDB cluster with no data
- No risk of breaking the original app's data
- You must manually migrate data if you want to copy records from the original (export/import or script)

<Tip>
If you need to carry data forward into a fork, export collections from the original app's MongoDB cluster and import them into the new one. See the [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) page for connection details.
</Tip>
